newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Strike shuts down Israeli seaports.
newsitem.headline: Strike shuts down Israeli seaports.

text.p: Israeli workers protesting against planned cuts in government spending staged a second day of strikes on Friday, shutting down seaports, officials said.
The strike closed Haifa, Ashdod and Eilat ports, and disrupted telephone services across Israel.
Leaders of the the Histadrut labour federation said strikes were planned in other sectors in the coming days to protest budget cuts which they said would erode workers' salaries.
Union leaders also threatened to stage a general strike on Tuesday when parliament is due to vote on the government's 1997 budget.

On Thursday all outgoing flights were cancelled at Israel's international Ben Gurion airport as a result of the strike. Incoming flights were allowed to land but airport workers did not unload baggage.

The government's 1997 budget proposal includes seven billion shekels ($2.15 billion) in spending cuts and new taxes and other revenue measures that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyhau has said are necessary to rein in the deficit.
The budget must be passed in parliament by the end of the month.
